defaults.permitted_development: Across Surrey, a side extension normally only falls within Class A if it is single storey, stays behind the principal elevation and does not exceed half the width of the original house. Width, parking loss and the effect of the flank wall usually decide whether it still reads as a modest addition.

rules.height_rules: Across Surrey, the usual side-extension fallback is an overall height of up to 4m, with eaves at or below 3m where any part sits within 2m of a boundary. Keeping the side roof low is usually what stops the flank wall becoming visually heavy.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate side-extension depth allowance in the way people often expect. The real test is whether the addition stays clearly subordinate to the original house and does not turn the side elevation into an oversized new wing.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Surrey, the key boundary checks are width, side-gap character, neighbour outlook and whether the addition creates an overbearing flank wall from the street or adjoining land.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the roof clearly secondary to the main house. A simple, low side roof is usually easier to defend than a taller form that competes with the original ridgeline.
rules.materials_rules: Materials should match or sit very closely with the existing house so the side addition reads as part of the dwelling rather than a bolt-on block.

rules.permitted_development: A side extension normally stays within permitted development only if it is single storey, clearly behind the principal elevation and comfortably within half the original-house width. rules.height_rules: The normal side-extension limit remains 4m overall, with eaves at or below 3m wherever any part is within 2m of a boundary. rules.depth_rules: Depth is judged less by a fixed metre rule than by whether the extension remains clearly subsidiary to the original side wall and does not read as an overlarge flank addition.
